svg.title: Where transport keys and records live
svg.desc: Only public keys cross the handshake. The client private key stays in that object’s memory; destroy clears local state. Server private keys come from trusted Secrets. Cache stores expiring client public keys, used request IDs and minute counters. Closing a manager neither deletes all shared records nor closes the application’s Cache connection.
svg.metadata: flowchart LR A["Client object memory"] B["Local SM2 key pair; server public key and session ID"] C["Server process / trusted Secret"] D["Server private-key ring; consistent versions across nodes"] E["Shared Cache owned by the application"] F["Client public keys: fixed TTL"] G["Used IDs: keep through replay protection window"] H["Two minute counters: quota resets on expiry"] A --> B C --> D E --> F E --> G E --> H classDef default fill:#edf3ff,stroke:#476aab,color:#172b4d,stroke-width:1.5px; classDef good fill:#e9f6ef,stroke:#28734e,color:#17452f,stroke-width:1.5px; classDef stop fill:#fff0f0,stroke:#af4040,color:#742b2b,stroke-width:1.5px; classDef pending fill:#fff6df,stroke:#a07827,color:#654b18,stroke-width:1.5px;

text.font-family: Noto Sans CJK SC,Noto Sans CJK JP,sans-serif
